title: Git working tree, staging, commits, branches, merging, pull requests, and conflict resolution
objectives: Map working tree, staging area, and commit to how Salesforce metadata source actually gets recorded.
Choose branches, pull requests, and merges for a metadata change rather than committing straight to the default branch.
Separate Git merge conflicts from Salesforce CLI source-tracking conflicts with the org.
Name files that must never be committed (org auth, secrets) while still treating the repository as the metadata source of truth.
diagnostic_question: Two teammates retrieve the same Flow, one commits on main, the other has uncommitted XML. A third has a source-tracking conflict with a sandbox. Which problem is Git, which is org sync, and what would you verify first?
definition: Git records snapshots of the DX project's metadata source. The working tree is the files you edit, the staging area (index) is what the next commit will include, and a commit is a recorded snapshot. Branches isolate work; merging and pull requests integrate it; conflicts appear when two snapshots both changed the same lines. Salesforce DX still treats that repository as the metadata source of truth, which is a different question from CLI source tracking against an org. ([Salesforce DX tooling](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_intro.htm); [Track Changes Between Your Project and Org](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_source_tracking.htm); [Git Basics](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Basics-Recording-Changes-to-the-Repository))
why_it_matters: A clean CLI deploy of a dirty Git history still ships the wrong XML. Interviewers listen for working tree versus staging versus commit, for pull requests as review of metadata, and for not confusing a Git conflict with an org source-tracking conflict.
sixty_second_explanation: Picture a rail switching yard. The working tree is cars sitting on the yard tracks (your files). Staging is coupling a consist for the next departure (git add). A commit is sealing that consist with a waybill. A branch is a parallel track. A pull request is the dispatcher reviewing before the consist joins the main line. A merge conflict is two trains claiming the same switch. Org source tracking is a different radio: local project versus sandbox, not Git versus Git.
deeper_explanation: Salesforce DX states that source code and metadata exist outside the org and that the version control system is the source of truth. Git is the usual VCS. Recording changes uses three trees: working directory (working tree), staging area, and commit history. You edit metadata source, git add to stage, git commit to snapshot. Unstaged retrieve output is not yet history. ([Salesforce DX tooling](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_intro.htm); [Git Basics](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Basics-Recording-Changes-to-the-Repository))

Branches isolate a LAB_ feature. Pull requests (host-specific: GitHub/GitLab/Azure Repos) are the review gate before merging into the integration branch. Merging combines histories. Metadata XML, especially large profile files, conflicts often; permission-set-sized diffs are easier (DEVOPS-008). Never force-push shared branches as a conflict 'fix' unless the team explicitly owns that danger.

Source tracking conflicts are not Git conflicts. CLI source tracking compares local project files with a scratch org or sandbox. Production never allows source tracking. Resolve org conflicts before deploy/retrieve when both sides changed the same component, or overwrite only when you are sure. Then commit the result so Git remains truth. ([Track Changes](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_source_tracking.htm))

Do not commit secrets, session files, or production data extracts. A DX project may include sample data; that is not a license to commit PII. .forceignore and .gitignore both matter: ignore local noise without hiding real metadata. Interview precision: merging a PR does not deploy; CI or a human still runs project deploy (DEVOPS-002/007).

mental_model.analogy: A rail switching yard: working tree = cars in the yard, staging = coupled consist, commit = sealed waybill, branch = parallel track, pull request = dispatcher review, merge conflict = two trains on one switch. Org source tracking is a different radio to the sandbox, not the yardmaster's ledger.
useful_mapping: working tree → files on disk including uncommitted retrieve output
staging / index → git add selection for the next snapshot
commit → immutable snapshot of staged metadata source
branch → movable pointer for a line of work
pull request → review before merge to the shared track
Git conflict → overlapping commits on the same lines
source-tracking conflict → local project versus org, not Git versus Git
merge ≠ deploy → history changed; the org still needs a metadata deploy
where_it_breaks: Git does not understand Salesforce metadata types; it diffs text.
Source tracking can be clean while Git is dirty, and the reverse.
Pull request tools are host products, not Git core.
The analogy does not encode package versioning or Apex tests.

claims.claim: In Salesforce DX, the version control system is the source of truth for source code and metadata outside the org.
claims.validation: Salesforce DX introduction and Project Setup.

claims.claim: Git records file states as working tree, staging area, and committed snapshot. git add stages; git commit records.
Source tracking compares the local project with a scratch org or sandbox and is used to identify and resolve conflicts before deploy/retrieve. It is not Git merge.
claims.validation: Track Changes Between Your Project and Org.

claims.claim: Merging Git history does not by itself deploy metadata to an org; a retrieve/deploy command or pipeline is still required.
claims.validation: DX treats VCS as truth and CLI as the org sync mechanism.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Git snapshots DX metadata: working tree, staging, commit. Branches and pull requests review XML before it becomes shared history. A Git conflict is not a CLI source-tracking conflict. Merge does not deploy.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I treat the repo as Salesforce's source of truth. I retrieve, then add and commit—not 'the org remembers.' I open a branch and PR for Flow/Apex XML. If two people edited the same layout, I merge as text and validate in a scratch org. If CLI reports conflicts with a sandbox, I resolve that org sync first, then commit. I never commit auth files. I never claim a merged PR updated production.

terminology.plain: The project files on disk, including edits not yet committed.
terminology.precise: Git's working directory copy of the repository files you edit. Retrieved metadata lands here before git add.
terminology.non_example: The org's Apex class with no local file.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Staging area: selected files for the next commit.
terminology.boundary: CLI retrieve writes the working tree, not a commit.

terminology.plain: The list of files the next commit will include.
terminology.precise: Also called the index. git add copies working-tree content into this snapshot-to-be.
terminology.non_example: sf project deploy start, which talks to an org.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Working tree: may still have unstaged edits.
terminology.boundary: Partial staging of XML is possible but easy to get wrong.

terminology.plain: A saved snapshot of staged files with a message.
terminology.precise: An immutable Git object recording a tree. History of metadata source lives here.
terminology.example: commit message: Add LAB_GateService retrieve from sandbox A.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Push: sending commits to a remote, still not a Salesforce deploy.
terminology.boundary: Amend rules are team policy; do not invent Salesforce behavior.

terminology.plain: A named line of commits for isolated work.
terminology.precise: A movable pointer to a commit. Feature branches keep LAB_ work off the integration branch until review.
terminology.non_example: A Salesforce sandbox name, which is an org, not a Git pointer.
terminology.boundary: Scratch org per branch is DEVOPS-004.

terminology.plain: A review of a branch before it merges into the shared history.
terminology.precise: A hosting-product workflow around Git branches. Used to review metadata diffs. Merging the PR is not a metadata deploy.
terminology.example: PR showing Flow XML plus Apex test, required reviewer, then merge.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: git pull: fetching and integrating a remote branch locally.

terminology.plain: Combining another branch's commits into this one.
terminology.precise: Creates a merge commit or fast-forward so histories join. Conflicts halt the merge until the working tree is resolved and committed.
terminology.example: Merging feature/lab-gate-service into main after PR approval.
terminology.non_example: sf project deploy start to UAT.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: rebase: alternative history rewrite; team policy.
terminology.boundary: Do not treat merge as production release.

terminology.plain: Editing the file so Git (or source tracking) no longer has two winners.
terminology.precise: Git conflicts are overlapping line changes in history. Source-tracking conflicts are local versus org. Resolve the right pair, then commit.
terminology.example: Two Flow XML <status> lines; keep the reviewed version, deploy to a scratch org, commit.
terminology.boundary: Profile XML conflicts are a reason to prefer permission sets (DEVOPS-008).

terminology.plain: The project file and the scratch/sandbox component both changed.
terminology.precise: CLI source tracking identifies conflicts between local project and org. Best practice: resolve before deploy/retrieve. Not a Git merge.
terminology.example: Layout edited in VS Code and in Setup; CLI reports a conflict.
terminology.non_example: Two Git branches both edited the layout and Git stops a merge.

when_to_use: When retrieved metadata sits in the working tree and must become a commit on a branch.
When two developers' commits conflict in Flow or layout XML and you must merge or rebase.
When a pull request is the review gate before metadata becomes shared history.
When CLI source tracking reports a conflict and you must not treat it as a Git merge conflict.
When deciding that merging the branch still requires a metadata deploy.
when_not_to_use: Do not use Git commits as a substitute for Salesforce CLI retrieve/deploy (DEVOPS-002).
Do not use a pull request as a change set; PRs do not move metadata into production by themselves.
Do not resolve org source-tracking conflicts with git merge tools aimed at the wrong copy pair.
Do not commit production data, session files, or secrets because the working tree happened to contain them.
Do not treat this topic as unlocked-package versioning (DEVOPS-005).

decision_table.signal: Retrieved XML is only on disk and must enter history.

decision_table.not: Leaving it unstaged and calling Git the source of truth.

decision_table.not: Including them so 'the project is complete.'

Confusing source-tracking conflicts with Git conflicts.
Committing everything in the working tree including .sfdx.
Using the sandbox name as if it were a Git branch.

options.D: Only if the sandbox is named main

interview_questions.question: Explain working tree, staging, and commit for Salesforce metadata.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Retrieve or edit files in the working tree. git add stages them. git commit snapshots staged metadata. Until commit, Git is not actually truth.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: DX says VCS is truth, so I show git status after retrieve. Unstaged Flow XML is only disk. I stage the intended files, not auth. I commit on a branch. I do not claim Salesforce invented Git; I map it onto metadata source.
interview_questions.example: LAB_BoardingFlow.flow-meta.xml unstaged after retrieve, then staged and committed on feature/lab-boarding.
tradeoffs: Partial add precision versus adding all of force-app
Small commits versus one giant retrieve
follow_ups: What does git status tell you?

interview_questions.question: How do branches and pull requests fit source-driven Salesforce work?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A branch isolates metadata commits. A pull request reviews the XML before merge. Merge still does not deploy to any org.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep feature work off main. Reviewers read Flow and Apex diffs. Required checks may run CLI tests (later topics). After merge, CI or a human deploys. I do not treat the PR as a change set.
interview_questions.example: PR for LAB_GateService plus test class, one reviewer, then deploy to a staging sandbox.

interview_questions.question: Two people edited the same layout. Git conflicts. What do you do?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Finish the merge in Git by choosing the correct XML, validate in a scratch org, commit the resolution. Do not use org ignore-conflicts as a Git tool.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at both sides as text. I may retrieve a known-good org copy if both are wrong. I run a deploy to a disposable org. I mention profile XML as a reason to stop storing broad profiles in the same way. I never force-push main to hide the conflict.
interview_questions.example: Conflict markers in LAB_Gate layout; keep the reviewed field order; deploy to scratch; commit.
tradeoffs: Layout in source versus rebuild in Setup

interview_questions.question: CLI says conflict, git status is clean. Diagnose.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: That is source tracking versus the scratch or sandbox, not a Git merge. Resolve the org pair, then commit if the local file changed.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I run preview commands. I decide whether Setup or the project should win. Production would not even offer this tracking. After resolution I verify git status because retrieve may dirty the working tree.
interview_questions.example: Layout changed in Setup while Git already had the last commit; retrieve after choosing org or local.
weak_answer_warnings: git merge to fix the sandbox

interview_questions.question: What must never go in the Salesforce metadata repo?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Secrets, org auth, session files, and production PII extracts. Sample LAB_ data may live with the DX project; personal data must not.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I review .gitignore and .forceignore. I fail a PR that adds sfdx auth. If it already landed, rotate. Metadata names can still be PII. CI gets secrets from a secret store, not from Git (DEVOPS-007).
interview_questions.example: Rejecting a commit of .sfdx/sfdx-config plus a production Contact.csv.
tradeoffs: Convenient local auth versus leak risk

interview_questions.question: A stakeholder says the pull request merged so UAT is updated. Your reply?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Merge updated Git, the source of truth. UAT updates only after a metadata deploy to that org. I will check the deploy job.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I keep DEVOPS-001 in play: we deployed metadata source, not records. I show the pipeline or the CLI report. If deploy failed tests, UAT is not updated despite a green GitHub merge.
interview_questions.example: main includes LAB_GateService; UAT Apex list still lacks it until sf project deploy start succeeds.
tradeoffs: Auto-deploy on merge versus gated deploy

interview_questions.question: git status is huge after a retrieve of profiles. How do you recover?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Do not commit the noise by default. Stage only intended components. Consider whether profiles belong in this repo shape at all.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Broad retrieves dirty unrelated XML. I use a tighter --metadata list next time. I unstage. I mention permission sets as a source-control-friendly authorization unit. I still commit real needed changes on a branch with a PR.
interview_questions.example: Retrieve of Profile:Admin rewrote thousands of lines; only LAB_ custom field permissions were intended.
tradeoffs: Narrow retrieve versus full org snapshot
follow_ups: How do unlocked packages treat profiles?
weak_answer_warnings: Commit all diffs to 'stay in sync'

interview_questions.question: Teach Git to an admin who only knows change sets, using the rail-yard analogy.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Change sets are a pallet between two docks. Git is the yard ledger of every car. Working tree, staging, commit, branch, PR, then a separate train (deploy) to an org.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not insult change sets; they still move metadata between related orgs. Source-driven work versions XML in Git so two sandboxes and production can share history. I warn that Git conflicts are text and that org tracking is another radio. I never say a PR replaces a change set deploy.
interview_questions.example: Admin retrieves a validation rule, commits on a branch, PR, merge, then CLI deploy to UAT instead of an outbound change set only.
tradeoffs: Related-org only versus any org you can auth
follow_ups: When are change sets still reasonable?
weak_answer_warnings: A pull request deploys to the org
